title: Shaders & the Rendering Pipeline
description: Discover how shaders control the final look of your objects and get a peek into the rendering flow.

slides.title: What is a Shader? 🖥️
slides.content:
# The Graphics Code

A **Shader** is a small program that runs on the GPU and determines how each pixel of a rendered object looks. It takes input (mesh, material properties, lights) and outputs the final color.

- Unity includes many built‑in shaders: **Standard**, **Unlit**, **Sprite‑Default**, **Particles**, etc.
- The **Standard Shader** is physically‑based (PBR) and is the default for 3D.
- **Unlit Shader** ignores lighting, useful for UI or flat‑colored objects.

You can also create custom shaders using **Shader Graph** (visual tool) or HLSL code.

options.text: Defines the shape of the object
Calculates how each pixel should be colored

quizData.explanation: Shaders determine the visual appearance of a surface by computing pixel colors.

slides.title: The Rendering Pipeline (Simplified) 🚦
slides.content:
# How a Triangle Becomes a Pixel

1. **Vertex Shader** – processes each vertex of the mesh (position transformations).
2. **Rasterization** – converts triangles into fragments (potential pixels).
3. **Fragment (Pixel) Shader** – computes the final color for each pixel, using material data and lighting.

Unity’s built‑in pipeline handles most of this automatically. The Shader you select in the material determines how the fragment shader behaves.

Later you might explore **URP** (Universal Render Pipeline) or **HDRP**, which provide different rendering features.

quizData.question: Which shader stage runs for each pixel?
quizData.explanation: The fragment shader (also called pixel shader) operates per pixel.

slides.title: Choosing a Shader 🎛️
slides.content:
# When to Use Which

- **Standard** – 3D objects that need full lighting (most game assets).
- **Unlit** – UI elements, minimap icons, or objects that always appear bright.
- **Sprite‑Default** – for 2D sprites.
- **Particles** – for particle systems.
- **Mobile‑Diffuse** – simpler shader for performance on mobile.

You switch the shader via the dropdown at the top of the material Inspector.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Preview Shader Changes

When you modify a material’s shader or properties, all objects using that material update in real‑time in the Scene view. Use this for quick visual iteration.
